title: Autonomous acceptance suite for OSS weights: sample-to-pin fastpath
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an autonomous acceptance pipeline that takes a community model weights tarball through deterministic sanity checks, lightweight conversion, canary profiling, and automatic pin recommendation so that compatible open-source LLMs can be fast-triaged and published to staging with minimal manual intervention.
background: Onboarding new community weights today requires a mix of manual steps: verifying manifests, running heavy end-to-end benchmarks, and human review to decide which variant to pin. This slows time-to-serve and creates a bottleneck for community-driven model additions. We need a reliable ‘fastpath’ to catch high-quality candidate models and surface lower-risk conversion recommendations to the runtime team and PMs.
goals: Automate initial ingest checks for provenance, license, and checksum parity
Perform deterministic conversion to Redwood runtime-compatible artifacts with fallback profiles (float16, q4_0)
Run a canary profiling stage (sample inference, KV-cache sizing, latency distribution) in a short window (<30 minutes)
Produce a machine-readable pin recommendation including variant, quantization profile, and expected p95 latency on target GPU family
Emit clear human-facing artifact: conversion log, telemetry snapshot, and a verification checklist for final sign-off
scope: Weights intake to recommended pin publish on staging only. This includes manifest validation, conversion via conversion-service, smoke inference tests, and profile publish to the onboarding dashboard. It does NOT include full production rollout, SLA validation, or legal license adjudication beyond manifest checks.
out_of_scope: Manual legal/license adjudication beyond automated manifest parsing
Full long-seq throughput stress testing (handled by bench-runner job)
Final production pinning and release notes publishing
detailed_steps: 1) Intake: watch uploads to s3://community-weights/ingest and validate manifest.yaml (model_name, commit SHA, license, tokenizer) and provenance signatures
2) Sanity checks: verify hash checksums, required files present (.pt/.safetensors, tokenizer, config). Fail fast with structured reasons
3) Lightweight conversion: spawn conversion-service job (image: redwood/converter:2026-03) to produce runtime bundle and a q4_0 candidate. Record conversion logs and artifact sizes

4) Sample inference smoke: run 10 short prompts (from curated prompt_set) through converted bundle on staging GPU (A100-small). Capture latency histogram, token output fingerprints vs reference (token overlap & deterministic checksum), and KV cache allocation behavior
5) Canary profiling: execute profiling harness to estimate steady-state p95 and memory utilization for sequences [32, 128, 512]. Use predictor model to extrapolate for larger batch sizes
6) Heuristic decision engine: apply rule set and ML scorer to recommend pin variant(s) and quantization setting or mark as manual review if thresholds violated
7) Publish: write profile JSON into onboarding-store and create a candidate entry in onboarding dashboard with links to artifacts and a suggested PR template for final pinning
8) Alerting: emit a short Slack summary to #model-onboard with pass/fail and quick links; if fail, include remediation hints (missing tokenizer, OOM during q4 conversion, non-deterministic outputs)
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid community weights bundle, the pipeline produces a staging candidate entry within 30 minutes
Conversion returns an artifact that the runtime can attempt to load (smoke load success) in >=90% of healthy cases
Canary profiling produces p95 latency estimate and memory footprint for three standard sequence lengths
Pin recommendation accuracy: when pipeline recommends 'serveable' the downstream runtime smoke load and simple eval set must pass at least 80% of tests
On failure, the pipeline surfaces clear, actionable reasons and attached conversion logs
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Converter and Runtime teams; aligned on conversion image and required manifest fields
2026-03-04: PoC converter job created (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-intake/pull/289). Basic conversion to runtime bundle succeeds for GPT-style weights
2026-03-06: Implemented manifest validator lambda and S3 event wiring. Test upload flow validated end-to-end in dev account

2026-03-08: Canary profiling harness (sample prompts + latency collector) integrated with staging runner. First canary run for llama2-7b-community completed; issues: tokenizer mismatch for one model (logging improved)
2026-03-10: Heuristic decision engine drafted. Need to finalize threshold values with PM and runtime team. Blocker: endpoint quotas on staging A100 cluster during peak hours
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest validator with edges: missing tokenizer, invalid license string, signature mismatch
Integration test: upload synthetic bundle to dev S3, assert pipeline creates candidate row and conversion artifact exists
Smoke inference tests: for each converted artifact run 10 deterministic prompts and assert token checksum matches reference
Canary profiling stability: run 3 repeated canary runs and ensure p95 variation < 20% for stable candidates
Chaos test: simulate conversion worker restart mid-conversion and verify idempotent retry behavior
rollback_plan: If the pipeline starts producing incorrect pins or causes stability regressions, disable the automatic recommendation step via feature flag (feature: onboarding.fastpath.autopin) and revert converter image to last-known-good tag (redwood/converter:2026-02-rc3). Re-run recent candidate conversions in safe/manual mode and notify runtime on-call.
risks: False-positives: pipeline may recommend serving for models with subtle correctness regressions (mitigation: conservative thresholds & manual audit for high-impact models)
Resource pressure: canary profiling uses staging GPU capacity; need quota throttles and backoff
Tokenizer mismatches between upstream checkpoints and conversion tooling leading to non-deterministic outputs
Security/provenance spoofing: reliance on manifest without human legal review could surface models with problematic licenses (mitigation: flag unknown license and require manual step)
qa_notes: Coordinate with SRE to reserve a dedicated staging slot for scheduled canary runs

Ensure telemetry includes conversion duration, peak memory, and tokenization mismatch rate
